assumptions: Horizon: expected month-12 footprint; 730 hours/month. No tax, development/on-call labor, domain registration or new on-prem hardware procurement is included.
Peak concurrency absent: assumed 2% of month-12 users (2); this is a usage hypothesis, not measured traffic.
RPS absent: assumed 50 requests/user/day averaged across the day (0.058 RPS); peak capacity still uses the concurrency hypothesis.
Data volume 10 GB assumed because absent; egress 1 GB/month assumed at 0.01 GB per year-12 user, minimum 1 GB; backup retention 1 months assumed.

Compute provisioning hypothesis: 50 RPS or 1000 active users per reference allocation; WebSocket capacity is included in the peak-concurrency replica floor, not charged again as per-connection sidecars. 2.25 vCPU/2-GiB-equivalent units include frontend/backend, auth, workers, inference and telemetry once. These are sizing assumptions requiring load tests, not capacity guarantees.

Billed duty 1–1; run polling workers with allocated CPU/minimum instances. Higher availability adds at least two application allocations and in-region database copies, but does not guarantee an SLA. Rate bands include headroom; do not interpret reference regions/proxies as exact local provider quotes.
Managed database: 1 vCPU/4 GiB reference primary and 1 failover copies in-region; no SLA is guaranteed. Auth/search/outbox share logical database capacity and are not billed as duplicate databases.

score_breakdown.reason: USD 214.64–525.95/month versus budget 500: fit 5 when upper bound fits, 3 when only lower fits, 1 within twice budget, otherwise 0. All selected services are included under disclosed assumptions.
Language familiarity 1.00/5 and implementation-complexity rubric 3.00/5; short delivery/beginner-complexity and manual Markdown-conversion penalties are explicit heuristics.
Static delivery avoids application writes; embedded-writer and growth triggers are ordinal review heuristics, not published capacity limits.
No latency SLA or measured framework throughput is credited; embedded-write concurrency is a review heuristic. Low-memory clients require measurement, not an assumed framework benchmark.
Operational burden 2/5+; no existing-system reuse bonus. Fewer self-operated systems are favored without DevOps. Additional service operating penalty 0.
Baseline configured controls: 3; explicit reviewed tenant isolation: 4. No certification/audit credit is assigned.

alternatives.why_not: A compatible plan tied on score; the published cost-upper-bound/operated-component/identifier tie-break selected the primary plan, not intrinsic product superiority.

backend.justification: Provides a python application runtime for the web_app profile. Language familiarity and delivery complexity were compared across compatible whole plans. Selected after supporting-service compatibility and whole-plan infrastructure cost scoring. Explicit critical warnings identify provisional data-flow/control exceptions.
tradeoffs: Business features, authentication and compatible database drivers must be configured; the framework alone is not the application.

tradeoffs: Data model, backup policy, licensing and release/driver compatibility need explicit review.

summary: modular_monolith recommendation selected from 49 complete compatible plans; month-12 infrastructure planning band USD 214.64–525.95/month.

warnings.message: 99.9% is a target, not a product guarantee. The cost model provisions redundancy assumptions; service terms, failover and workload behavior still require verification.
Upper estimate USD 525.95/month exceeds USD 500; stated usage/price assumptions determine whether it fits.

Planning bands combine published reference rates and explicitly authored allowances; they are not regional provider quotes or measured workload capacity. Validate sizing, merchant/SMS eligibility, storage, requests and current tariffs before purchase.
